To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: [p05]
Cc: none
Subject: none

I'm a neighbour, not an engineer on a job here — no formal assessment, just what I could see from the pavement opposite at 7 this morning. Please take it as a neighbour's read, nothing more.

Mick, I would ask you not to go in at 9. Propping a roof from underneath with a loose stack overhead is the worst place to stand: the front floors may be loaded with fallen debris and nobody knows the load path now. Nor the loft at 43, for the same reason.

What I saw: at 41, about 1.2m of stack still standing, leaning towards 43, pots gone and the mortar washed out at the base — that could go in more wind (gusts again this afternoon). At 43, a hole of roughly 2–3 square metres in the front roof slope, debris in the front bedroom, a stepped crack from the bay head up to the first floor window cill, 5–10mm wide, and the bay head looking dropped by around 20mm. Loose slates are sitting on the gutter line of 43 and 45, directly over the footway.

Priya's two questions. Pavement: the tape is only across the front garden of 43, not the pavement, and loose slates could come down onto it. Please use the other side of the road until the council's dangerous structures officer has been and says otherwise — that includes the school run to St Dunstan's. Out-of-hours dangerous structures is via the main council number; they know already, but nobody has closed the footway, so please keep at them.

Mrs Doherty: not my decision, but I would not sleep in the front room tonight, and it would be better if she went to family until 45 has been checked. 45's own front wall looked undamaged, though I couldn't see the party wall from the front.

JoJo's cousin isn't wrong that terraces are robust in general — but this is a damaged one, and that's a different thing.

---

To: dm:Gary_41
Replying to: [d01]
Cc: none
Subject: none

Thanks for the message, and sorry for the worry. Nothing has gone on the forum and nothing will until we've spoken. Can I call you before 8.15? I want to be clear about 9 o'clock, and I'm on a client call then.

Two things. I won't say anything publicly about the chimney breasts without your agreement. And I can't advise you on the removal, or on what the insurers will do — that needs someone with the right cover and the paperwork in front of them, not a forum opinion. Do talk to your insurer early, and I'd not let anyone start work at 41 until an engineer with cover has looked at it.
